::: {#exm-digit-count}
#### Counting digits

Define a function $d$ on the natural numbers (@def-natural-numbers) by

$$
d(n) =
\begin{cases}
1 & \text{if } n \le 9,
\\ 1 + d\paren{\floor{n / 10}} & \text{if } n \ge 10,
\end{cases}
$$

where $\floor{n / 10}$ is the floor (@def-floor) of $n / 10$, which is $n$ with its last decimal digit removed.
The first line is the base case and the second is the recursive rule (@def-recursive-definition).
For $n \ge 10$, the input $\floor{n / 10}$ is at least 1 and at most $n / 10$, which is less than $n$,
so the recursive rule uses a smaller input, but usually not $n - 1$.
For example,

$$
\ba
d(2026)
&= 1 + d(202)
\\&= 1 + 1 + d(20)
\\&= 1 + 1 + 1 + d(2)
\\&= 1 + 1 + 1 + 1
\\&= 4,
\ea
$$

and 2026 has 4 digits.

:::
